Danube Cycle Path: Passau to Vienna
Austria · River towns & vineyards
325 km · 6–8 daysEasy–moderate · paved paths & short road sectionsMay–June / September · Vienna VIE or Munich MUC
Details & links
Ride downstream through Upper Austria and the Wachau to Vienna. Plan roughly 45–65 km on riding days; hire, inns and rail connections are plentiful in the main towns. The full Austrian EuroVelo 6 section continues beyond Vienna: this distance describes the Passau–Vienna itinerary, not the entire international route. Check flood-related closures and ferry timetables. The photograph shows the Wachau section.

Loire à Vélo: Cuffy to Saint-Brevin
France · Châteaux & riverside villages
About 620 km end to end · 10–14 daysEasy–moderate · paths & quiet roadsMay–June / September · Nantes NTE or Paris + rail
Details & links
The 900 km network includes loops and connections; the main end-to-end ride is about 620 km. Plan 40–65 km daily, with shorter days for castles. Follow official signage and use Accueil Vélo accommodation and rental listings; summer beds and one-way hires need booking. Not every segment is segregated from traffic. The regional vineyard photograph illustrates the Loire setting rather than a specific cycle-path segment.

Amsterdam & Waterland day loop
Netherlands · City lanes to polder villages
Plan 30–50 km · 1 dayEasy · paved paths with busy urban junctionsApril–September · Amsterdam AMS
Details & links
Choose an out-and-back or loop in the official Bike City route planner; 30–50 km is a suggested day plan, not the length of one signed route. City-bike hire is widespread and village cafés make breaks easy. Wind can make a flat ride feel strenuous. Follow local cycling rules, give way at junctions and watch tram tracks; this is not a traffic-free city tour. The photograph shows Amsterdam, the starting base.

Otago Central Rail Trail
New Zealand · Historic railway & big inland skies
152 km · 3–5 daysEasy / Grade 1 · unsealed gravel rail trailOctober–April · Queenstown ZQN or Dunedin DUD
Details & links
Ride Clyde to Middlemarch through former railway tunnels, bridges and small towns. A 30–50 km daily plan leaves room for stops; specialist operators offer bike hire, shuttles and luggage transfers, and accommodation is spread along the trail. Book ahead in busy periods. Expect exposed wind, temperature swings and gravel rather than asphalt; bring lights for tunnels. The photograph shows Central Otago's wider landscape.

Great Glen Cycle Way
United Kingdom · Canal, forest & Loch Ness
About 120–124 km · 2–4 daysModerate–demanding · towpaths, forest tracks & road linksMay–September · Inverness INV or Glasgow + rail
Details & links
Connect Fort William with Inverness along a bicycle-suitable Great Glen alignment. Distances vary with the chosen cycling variant. Do not assume the walking Way is identical to the bike route: some steep or narrow walking segments need alternatives. Use the operator's current cycling itinerary or GPX, a suitable mountain or robust gravel bike, and pre-book hire and luggage arrangements. Rain, midges and remote stretches matter more than the headline distance.

Planning notes & sources

  • Daily distances and trip durations are planning ranges, not official completion targets. Add rest, sightseeing and bad-weather days; assess fitness and route elevation independently.
  • Easy does not mean risk-free. Check current route GPX, closures, traffic exposure, bicycle suitability and helmet requirements. Rail-trails may be unsealed; mountain-bike alignments can differ from walking paths.
  • Airport codes identify useful gateways, not guaranteed direct transfers. Reserve bike hire, luggage transport and accommodation; verify airline bicycle carriage separately.
  • Official tourism, park and route sources are linked on the cards. Reviewed 15 September 2026. Photographs are existing locally hosted Wikimedia assets; credits identify the original file and licence. Regional photographs illustrate the setting, not a guaranteed view or exact route alignment.
